stem: Why is regular ophthalmic screening essential for children with oligoarticular JIA even when they are in remission?

options.text: Uveitis is typically asymptomatic until damage occurs
The arthritis and eye disease always flare at the same time
Medications used for arthritis cause most eye damage
Only symptomatic children are at risk for vision loss

explanation: Children often do not complain of symptoms like blurry vision or photophobia until significant long-term complications have already developed.
rationale: Think about whether a child would notice or report the early stages of this eye condition.

optionExplanations.A: Children often do not complain of symptoms like blurry vision or photophobia until significant long-term complications have already developed.
optionExplanations.B: The lecture specifically notes that the course of uveitis does not parallel the disease course of the arthritis.
optionExplanations.C: While some meds have side effects, the primary concern described is the inflammatory process of uveitis itself.
optionExplanations.D: Asymptomatic children are at high risk, which is why screening is mandatory regardless of clinical complaints.

source.hint: Think about whether a child would notice or report the early stages of this eye condition.
